_what_this_is: The REQUIRED status contexts on this repo's default branch, as read back from the GitHub branch-protection API. Committed as a fixture because the floor tier is stdlib-only and offline: it cannot call the API. Consumed by tests/test_ci_enforcement_floor.py (INV-3, INV-5).
_why_it_exists: INV-3 used to credit ANY workflow that triggers on master. That conflates 'a gate that CAN run' with 'a gate that IS required' — the exact distinction PR #15 argued for in prose and then failed to encode. Re-adding --ignore=tests/test_smoke_e2e.py to the REQUIRED unit-tests job still passed INV-3, because the non-required smoke-test.yml got the credit. Only a context in this file can make a test file 'covered'.
_staleness_contract: This file is a CLAIM about a mutable remote setting. It goes out of date silently, so it carries its own expiry: observed_at + max_age_days. Past that, INV-3 and INV-5 fail as NOT-OBSERVED (never pass) until someone re-runs refresh_command and updates observed_at. A stale fixture must not be able to certify anything.

_trust_root._what_this_is: The honest boundary of what the offline floor tier can certify from this file. Codex review of PR #15: expiry and 'the job exists' cross-checks prove this file is FRESH and COHERENT; they do not prove branch protection actually requires these contexts. Per DONE.md floor entry 9(d) a property that was not observed must not be rendered as a success, so the boundary is declared here rather than left implicit.
proven: the fixture is well-formed, names this repo's default branch, and is within its declared expiry (INV-5)
every required GitHub-Actions context listed here is produced by a job that exists in the workflow tree, so none is a phantom that could never go green
every test file in the repo is collected by a job whose check name appears in this list (INV-3)
no deselection filter (-k / --ignore / --deselect) hides a test file from such a job
assumed: that this file matches what branch protection ACTUALLY requires on master right now. It is a committed claim about a mutable remote setting. If it were wrong, or edited to add 'MCP server end-to-end smoke test', every offline check would still pass and INV-3 would credit a job that gates nothing. This is demonstrated on purpose by tests/test_ci_enforcement_floor.py::test_fixture_manipulation_is_undetectable_offline.
_trust_root.why_irreducible_here: The floor tier contract is stdlib-only and offline. Reading branch protection requires an authenticated GitHub API call with admin scope, which no floor check can make. The trust root cannot be discharged in this tier — only moved.
_trust_root.verified_by: human refresh via refresh_command, recorded in observed_at
_trust_root.how_to_make_it_live: A scheduled privileged job (PAT with administration:read) that calls refresh_command and fails on any drift from this file would move the trust root from 'a human remembered' to 'a job checks daily'. Proposed, NOT implemented: the default GITHUB_TOKEN cannot read branch protection, so it needs a secret this PR does not create. Note that cross-checking the check-runs POSTED on a PR is not a substitute — posted and required are different properties, and a job can post while being non-required.
_trust_root.max_age_days_is_a_floor_not_a_guarantee: Within the expiry window this file is trusted, not verified. Protection can change the day after a refresh and nothing here will notice until observed_at ages out.

_not_required_but_triggers_on_master.smoke-test.yml / MCP server end-to-end s: runs pytest tests/test_smoke_e2e.py and DOES trigger on push+pull_request to master since 6c3ec67, but it is NOT in required_checks. It therefore credits NOTHING in INV-3. This is the entry that made Codex's probe pass.
_not_required_but_triggers_on_master.security_scan.yml / bandit, dependency-a: also triggers on master, also not required, also credits nothing as direct branch-protection contexts.
_not_required_but_triggers_on_master.unit-tests.yml / unit-tests: IS in required_checks and now aggregates the blocking Bandit, pip-audit, and TruffleHog scans so those scanner failures can block under an existing required context even though the standalone security_scan.yml job contexts are not required.

_security_scan_required_context_limitati.why_not_changed_in_code: GitHub branch protection is a mutable remote setting, not a repository file. Making Bandit static analysis, Dependency vulnerability audit, or Check for committed secrets directly required needs the refresh_command-class GitHub API operation with admin-scoped credentials; this PR cannot safely or honestly claim to change that setting offline.
_security_scan_required_context_limitati.offline_floor_boundary: The floor can prove the fixture is fresh and coherent with workflow job names, and can prove that unit-tests contains the aggregate scanner steps. It still assumes this fixture matches live branch protection until a human or privileged drift job refreshes it.

_caveats_not_waived.enforce_admins_false: An admin can push straight to master and bypass all five contexts. INV-3/INV-5 certify what gates an ORDINARY PR; they do not certify that master cannot be written past.
_caveats_not_waived.no_required_reviews: required_pull_request_reviews is null on master. Status checks are the only gate.
_caveats_not_waived.app_id_not_verified_per_run: app_id is recorded from the protection payload so INV-5 can tell a GitHub-Actions context (must be produced by a job in this repo) from an external app's context (Aikido, app_id 898896 — produced outside the workflow tree and therefore exempt). INV-5 does not verify that the external app actually posts.
